forces: Mode A proof of concept in #128 met all utility, coverage, validation, and privacy thresholds, but L1 (envelope size budget of <= 256 B) was unmet (measured 357 B max, 354 B median over 1,112 interactions) (#498).
The structural floor of a minimal ClientEvidenceEnvelope v1 in Mode A with zero claims, 32-64 byte hex nonce, and fixed provenance block is 323-359 B, making 256 B physically unreachable as written.
Option 1 (omitting provenance from envelopes) would break ADR-009, violate frozen contract security-audit requirements, and destabilize ClientEvidenceEnvelope v1 schema.

Option 2 (revising L1 threshold to <= 384 B) accurately reflects the structural floor plus 27 B headroom, preserves frozen contracts, keeps browser and collector implementations stable, and resolves the PoC outcome to GO.
The revised L1 threshold must be verified by both the synthetic Mode A proof-of-concept harness and regression tests in @bloodtrail/client-evidence-browser.

security_justification.audit_integrity: Preserves audit event integrity. Admitted client evidence is linked solely as low-assurance correlation context under client_claim trust without altering server audit fields.
security_justification.authentication_or_authorization: Does not touch authentication, authorization, credentials, or enforcement paths; client evidence remains forbidden from reaching risk models or auth decisions.
security_justification.authority_provenance: Decision #498 explicitly records delegated authority under #118: decision_source = 'delegated to Claude by the owner, 2026-09-11; not a human owner decision'.
security_justification.concurrency: Synthetic proof-of-concept and browser SDK operations execute statelessly or under explicit single-use nonce ledgers with no asynchronous race conditions.
security_justification.confidentiality: The envelope inventory remains strictly minimal and closed (UUID v4, interaction kind, timestamp, provenance, nonce); no PII, URLs, cookies, or storage identifiers are admitted.
security_justification.cryptography: Preserves standard cryptographic generation of 128-bit random interaction IDs via crypto.getRandomValues and 32-to-64 character hexadecimal server nonces.
security_justification.error_disclosure: Diagnostics and rejection classes report bounded constants (bounds, version, replay, fabrication) without reflecting untrusted payloads or internal system state.
security_justification.external_security_integration: The browser package makes no network requests and imports no runtime dependencies; the envelope is transmitted solely by the host application's existing channels.
security_justification.fail_posture: Fails closed. Ingress continues to reject oversized envelopes exceeding bounds, unknown versions, unadmitted bindings, and replayed or substituted nonces deterministically.
security_justification.lifecycle: Revises the synthetic evaluation metric L1 from <= 256 B to <= 384 B, concluding the Mode A evaluation phase with GO while maintaining all stop criteria.
security_justification.mutation_ownership: Mutations are strictly confined to specification, decision record, proof-of-concept harness, and browser package tests; no production runtime code is mutated.
security_justification.privacy_transformation: Enforces zero inventory violations and zero identifier reuse across distinct interactions, prohibiting browser fingerprinting or persistent cross-interaction tracking.
security_justification.resource_retention: Preserves ephemeral capture scope; no interaction identifiers or client claims are persisted in browser storage APIs (localStorage, IndexedDB, cookies).
security_justification.retry_or_redelivery: Retried requests inside an interaction reuse the interaction identifier without generating new envelopes or re-spending burned nonces.
security_justification.trust_boundary: Preserves existing trust boundaries without alteration. All claims in ClientEvidenceEnvelope v1 remain strictly bounded at client_claim trust and are mapped fail-closed without elevating to server evidence.
